## Recent Reflexion (last 2 sessions)

## S168 (2026-09-08) — the four bugs he reported while playing, his boss stats, and the first two boss skills

- The reducer was innocent and that is exactly why the bug survived. `raidParity.test.ts` had been
  proving bot and human raids byte-identical for sessions, and it was RIGHT. Neither half of the
  owner's complaint lived there: one was arithmetic (a tower's component is too small for R76 to
  protect) and one was the input picker (a 34 px creature radius swallowing an 8 px bond click).
  A green test that is true can still be pointing away from the defect.

- A guard that fires is worth more than a guard that passes, and I nearly built the second one. My
  new letterbox rule flagged the Kraken's DIE row — three columns at the frame edge. The tempting
  fix was to raise the pixel tolerance; the right one was to require a MINIMUM BAR WIDTH, because a
  sliver is not a bar. Loosening the tolerance would have hidden small real bars forever.

- Fixing the reported defect un-masked the one underneath it. Removing the scarab's black bars made
  `check:atlas` go RED on a size mismatch — because the bars had been inflating the bbox that
  `normaliseStateScale` measures. That WAS the owner's S165 "walk row too small" complaint, closed
  three sessions ago without the cause ever being found. Two reports, one root cause.

- I looked at the frames instead of re-rolling. The regenerated Kraken clip was still pillarboxed,
  and the cheap move was another generation at his expense. Extracting a contact sheet showed veo
  had also ZOOMED despite a static-camera instruction — so no prompt was going to fix it, and
  `sampleStart` did. He had just said "dont waste my money"; the way to honour that was to look.

- S167's recommendation would have worked and still been wrong. It proposed widening the
  deferred-death batch so one hook catches every kill. It does — and it also hands every
  turret-killed creature a free posthumous swing, because deferral exists so a creature lands its
  committed strike. A death skill does not need a death hook; it needs to notice an ABSENCE.

- My own first cut of that had a hole, and I found it by asking who ELSE deletes a boss. A player
  raid is dispatched from main.ts's intent drain, OUTSIDE `runHostTick`, so a within-tick snapshot
  never saw it alive. The question "what runs outside the thing I am bracketing" is cheaper than
  the bug.

- Two of my own new tests failed honestly and BOTH were real. The tier-3 tower emitted exactly once
  forever (a missing `sourceSpawnerId` routed the spawn into the Voltkin one-per-type gate), and my
  test harness advanced `w.tick` twice per iteration. I nearly "fixed" a clock bug that did not
  exist. A trace of the actual arm settled both in one step; reading the diff would not have.

- A negative control is two minutes and it is the only thing that makes a green suite evidence.
  Disabling the explosion reds exactly three assertions; neutering the heal reds exactly two. Both
  run, neither assumed.

- An assertion that has to be weakened is worth more written down than silently edited. I claimed
  BACK TO MAIN was the topmost surface on screen; `top-centre-plate` sits three pixels above it.
  The claim worth pinning was about the right-hand column, and the walk-back is now a comment.

- The panel was lying and only a real network call could prove it. He was told his TURN credentials
  were "wrong or expired"; the verdict keyed on `relay === 0` with NO error code required, and the
  gather loop discarded the one code that means "unreachable". An actual RFC-5766 Allocate against
  the shipped relay returned 0x0103 SUCCESS. An accusation in the UI needs evidence behind it, the
  same way a claim in a commit message does.

## S167 (2026-09-08) — the tier-9 boss tower + its six bosses (PROTOCOL 44), the art that had never been drawn, and a guard that was only ever a comment

- A comment claiming a guard is not a guard. stats.ts had cited statsLadder.test.ts BY NAME since
  S151; the file never existed. I read it, believed the owner's 1..12 range was enforced, and
  shipped bosses at five times the ceiling with every gate green.

- A negative control found my own new test vacuous - twice in one session. The 5x-overkill assertion
  measured against max(pool) OF THE SET IT WAS JUDGING, so an inflated boss raised its own bar.

- Art that ships is not art that draws. t3TowerAtlasBase had ZERO production callers for two
  sessions. An existence test cannot tell 'present' from 'used'.

- The client-local pattern solved three different problems: when the entity is GONE from the sim, a
  renderer-owned animation is not a compromise, it is the only correct place.

- Stop when the design needs the owner. The zombie death explosion looked like a free win until I
  traced the death path and found defender kills bypass the deferred-death batch entirely.
